newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Economic upswing for Asia-Pacific to continue - PECC.
newsitem.headline: Economic upswing for Asia-Pacific to continue - PECC.

text.p: The economies of the Pacific region will grow slightly faster in 1997 and 1998 while inflation will continue to decline, the Pacific Economic Cooperation Council (PECC) think-tank said in its annual forecast released on Tuesday.
"The Asia Pacific region is forecast to achieve a weighted average real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of 4.1 percent for 1997 and 1998, following four percent growth in 1996," the PECC said.
"The best way to describe such an outcome would be as a high and sustainable plateau," it added.
It noted much of the growth acceleration in 1996 was the result of stronger economic performances in Japan and the US.
"Excluding Japan and the the U.S., real GDP growth is expected to jump from 5.0 to 5.5 percent in 1997 and to 5.7 percent in 1998."
The forecast said the excellent inflation performance of 1996 was not a fluke. The weighted average rate of inflation fell to 3.6 percent from 5.2 percent, with Russia excluded, the PECC said.
"Further improvement in inflation is forecast," it added.
The PECC said there were some economic problems in the region, "But they appeared to have captured all of the media attention."

Turning to individual economies, the PECC said, "Inflation is forecast to rise in both Indonesia and Vietnam, but the levels are well within the range that both economies have been able to manage in the past."
But it said, "...the financial situation in Russia is so unsettled that price stability is not in view."

"Monetary authorities can correctly claim victory against inflation, but they cannot end the fight. While they are responsible to prevent a resurgence, however, they are getting help from developments in the world econmy,' it said.
The PECC is a non-governmental organisation devoted to economic cooperation in the Pacific Rim. The report covered 20 countries.
